recordDecisions.title: Tight value-oracle approximability of submodular facility location
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Elmachtoub, Natura and Neuwohner report that homogeneous metric submodular facility location has no o(log log |C|) approximation using polynomially many value-oracle queries, even with unlimited computation and matroid-rank opening costs. This matches the known O(log log |C|) upper bound up to constants. The natural configuration LP has a matching Theta(log log |C|) integrality gap.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The paper credits ChatGPT 6.1 Astra with an initial no-constant-factor proof and subsequent conversations with Claude Opus5.5 and ChatGPT6.1 Astra with the tight lower bound; the humans digested, simplified and wrote the arguments.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit the symmetry-gap extension, replication and oracle indistinguishability, and distinguish homogeneous opening costs, value-oracle query hardness and configuration-LP gaps from computational NP-hardness or heterogeneous facility costs. Check the matching2024 upper-bound hypotheses. Independent proof verification is not established. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: First arXiv submission, distinguished from later revision and discovery dates.

recordDecisions.title: Single generation of transformation-group C*-algebras
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Elliott, Li and Niu report that C(X) crossed with a finitely generated discrete amenable group is singly generated when X is nonempty compact metrizable and the action is free, minimal, and has the uniform Rokhlin property and Cuntz comparison of open sets. This includes every free minimal Z^d action for d>=1, without imposing zero mean dimension. It does not assert density of generators or a generator-rank bound.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The primary acknowledgement says the work was carried out using ChatGPT; exact model and theorem-level contribution are unspecified.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit tower/complement recovery in norm, the finite-frame identity and countable assembly; smallness in measure is not smallness in norm. Establish original mathematical AI allocation and novelty, distinguishing this action-based result from3999 and3970. Do not omit finite generation, URP or comparison hypotheses. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: First arXiv submission, distinguished from later revision and discovery dates.

recordDecisions.title: Equivariant noncommutative crepant resolutions and maximal modifying modules
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Hirano reports that for a Cohen–Macaulay normal domain containing a field, a small finite-group action of invertible order transfers equivariant noncommutative crepant resolutions and cluster-tilting modules to the invariant ring. The paper also treats equivariant maximal modification algebras, derived equivalence for Gorenstein MMAs of three-dimensional Q-Gorenstein Cohen–Macaulay rings, and index-two terminal singularities.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Version2 explicitly says ChatGPT6 was used only for reference searches and finding typos and errors in version1. Origination remains the author’s.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Determine which errors were mathematical and which corrections were adopted; do not infer AI discovery or material proof generation from the acknowledgement. Audit small-action, invertibility, Gorenstein and dimension restrictions against the corrected v2. First submission was October8; v2 and the explicit disclosure are dated October14. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: First arXiv submission, distinguished from later revision and discovery dates.

recordDecisions.title: A sharp universal support criterion for symmetric sub-Gaussian laws
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: JD Jones reports that a zero-symmetric real probability law with 0<a<=|X|<=b is strictly sub-Gaussian with its actual variance whenever b/a<=sqrt(3)+sqrt(2), sharply over all such laws. In normalized squared support [3-sqrt(6),3+sqrt(6)], the package gives the sharp eighth-order MGF gap, fourth-contact rigidity and an attained W1 bound for squared laws at every feasible fourth-cumulant deficit.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The owner credits human-directed GPT6 Astra/Codex proof and exact-certificate development, with a GPT6 Pro consultation supplying sharp-gap and global-transport arguments.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check arbitrary-law endpoint reduction, moment-tail and Bernstein certificates, exact sharp constants and squared-law W1 equality cases. Compare against Kantorovich and classical strict-sub-Gaussian criteria. Some general-interval, higher-Wasserstein and unsquared-law statements are written supplements, not selected formal endpoints; no human specialist review is claimed. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Depth-labeled substitution and interpolation in Sacchetti modal logics
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For every positive n, JD Jones reports that arbitrary simultaneous formula substitution controlled by atom and depth label preserves wGL_n theoremhood exactly when c(k+n)=c(k) for every positive depth k. Labeled interpolation properties are equivalent to their corresponding ordinary interpolation properties together with that periodicity condition. Further results classify period spectra, boxed-atom implications and composition, and preserve size and modal depth when transferring a supplied interpolant.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Primary disclosure credits GPT6/GPT6 Pro through human-directed Codex with mathematical arguments, Lean proofs and review.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit necessity countermodels and the positive-depth/root distinction, arbitrary target formulas, substitution composition and syntax-size claims. Ordinary interpolation existence theorems and algorithms remain explicit external inputs; the package does not prove them. Establish novelty relative to Sierra Miranda–Studer, Iwata and Kurahashi; agent reviews are not independent human review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Finite counterexamples to a restricted-sumset inverse theorem
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The owner reports that in Z/13Z the sets A={0,1,3,4,5,6,10}, B={0,1,4,6} satisfy the stated size and restricted-sumset equality hypotheses of Li–Liang2609.10148v2 TheoremA/3.1, but neither is an arithmetic progression. A separate Z/11Z example contradicts the stated lower bound of Lemma3.2. These are counterexamples to v2 as written, not a replacement inverse classification.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The maintainer explicitly credits GPT6/Codex with exact search, Lean construction and statement auditing; finite Python enumeration is discovery support, not a proof premise.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently match every v2 hypothesis and cyclic-progression convention to the finite witnesses; check whether later revisions repair the claims and whether a missing hypothesis explains either example. The source authors have not endorsed the counterexamples. Universal paper statements are not separately encoded; the formal endpoints certify witnesses. No untrusted program was executed. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Connected counterexamples to exact color-critical two-eigenvalue bounds
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For F=K5 minus an edge, the owner reports that joining K(s,s,s) and K4 by one bridge gives a connected F-free graph for every integer s>=3, with m=3s²+7 and lambda1²+lambda2²>4m/3 by an explicit positive rational gap. Arbitrarily large edge counts refute the exact forms of KKP Conjecture1.16 and Li–Liu–Zhang Conjecture5.4, not their strengthened asymptotic counterparts.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The pinned primary metadata credits GPT6 Codex with AI-assisted proof development and exact integer-vector certificates, reusing attributed BN spectral lemmas.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: The informal manuscript is private and cannot be independently read; audit the public finite graph, ordered adjacency eigenvalues, F-freeness and rational compression certificate. Check the original conjectures and the bounded excess versus asymptotic statements. No novelty/priority claim or independent human expert review is made; registration is not proof acceptance. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary registration unless an earlier public archive is pinned; earlier repository visibility remains to be established.

recordDecisions.title: An edge-localized two-eigenvalue bound
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The owner reports that every finite noncomplete simple graph with at least two vertices satisfies lambda1²+lambda2² <= sum over unordered edges e of 2(1-1/c(e)), where c(e) is the largest clique containing that edge. Connectedness is unnecessary. This is the literal KKP Conjecture1.15, stronger in localization than the global clique-number statement already in1308.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The primary metadata credits GPT6 Codex with proof adaptation and local formalization using Bradač’s scalar compression and Shengtong Zhang’s BN completely-positive spectral lift.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit the scalar edge-clique certificate and transfer to the two largest ordered eigenvalues. Establish whether AI produced a new mathematical proof or only formalized an existing deduction, and whether the claimed localization had already been proved. Do not count the inherited BN theorem again or extend to complete graphs; mechanical receipts need exact-commit checking. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Finite observations and recognition of the compact Albert algebra
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: MacGregor reports a local two-class reconstruction of labeled compact-real Albert frame triples from27 pair and27 triple traces in a fixed20-dimensional chart, distinguished by a degree-nine scalar Phi. Nonzero Phi gives generation by1,x,y,z. Recognition results require either a supplied tangent metric/full-curvature equivalence or exact finite-word inner-product/product-norm tables. These do not assert a global orbit classification or approximate-table recognition.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Primary authorship metadata says AI systems generated mathematical arguments, Lean code and exposition under Robert MacGregor; retained labels include GPT6 Astra and Claude, with additional owner-reported Gemini4 Argon and Claude Fable5 labels.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check local whole-fiber classification and chart assumptions, the full Phi derivative, generation implication and exact recognition hypotheses. Compare against Iltyakov, Glennie and cubic-Jordan reconstruction; no novelty is asserted. This compact-real package is distinct from1657’s split rational invariant-field claim. Checker results are for pre-comment-revision source; no independent human review is established. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: The linear MDS conjecture over every even-order finite field
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Kumar reports the exact maximum length of a k-dimensional linear MDS code over a finite field of even order q, for2<=k<=q: q+2 for k=3 or k=q-1, and q+1 otherwise, including attainment. The proof claims a common-height/envelope and characteristic-two colon-ideal obstruction. It says nothing about odd-order fields, nonlinear codes or classification of extremizers.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The owner explicitly says Pranava Kumar devised the informal mathematical argument without automation. Claude assisted its original Lean translation; Claude Opus5.5 later ported the development. AI discovery is not claimed.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit the envelope normalization, common-height compatibility and colon-ideal dimension bound against the actual code/arc statement. The source’s literature survey is not exhaustive after2019; establish novelty and historical priority for the full even case. Distinguish a new human theorem with AI-assisted proof translation from material AI origination. Formal verification and original mathematical AI contribution remain separate.  No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Conditional exact-rank five, six and seven elliptic-curve constructions
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Aronow and Lopatto’s owner package reports infinitely many geometric isomorphism classes of rational elliptic curves of each exact Mordell–Weil rank5,6,7 conditional in Lean on an explicit generic finite-complexity prime-pattern asymptotic. Literal admissibility checks, two-isogeny descent, actual point-group ranks, finite generation and infinitely many rational j-invariants are in the reported formal deductions. The analytic theorem itself is not formalized.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The metadata attributes Lean proof construction and checks to GPT6 Codex. Its source manuscript’s author note says the text except that note is machine-written under human supervision; exact original mathematical allocation is not established.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Read and independently audit the supplied manuscript, local-density normalization, prime-power removal and exact descent ranks. Do not call the Lean result unconditional or identify algebraic and analytic rank. Public manuscript identity/priority is not established by the private upload digest; distinguish source prose supervision from review of this Lean project. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Distinguishing planar Brownian images of time sets and measures
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Troscheit reports mutual singularity of planar Brownian image laws for s-Frostman probability time measures on [0,1], with 0<s<1, when their normalized expected correlation profiles have a nonvanishing limsup difference, including the stated lattice versus non-lattice self-similar class under the open set condition and dimension restrictions. In a fixed-dimension two-contraction family, each parameter has finitely many possible exceptions, and sufficiently small dimensions give pairwise separation. Minkowski-neighborhood reconstruction transfers specified measure-law distinctions to compact image sets. Equal profiles need not identify the original measure.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The primary paper says LLMs performed part of the two-contraction calculations and drafted much Lean code; the arguments and ideas are human-created, with some influence from formalization. Owner metadata names Claude and GPT6.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Establish which calculations and proof changes were AI contributions; audit profile asymptotics, mutual-singularity quantifiers, small-dimension restrictions and Minkowski reconstruction. The formalization proves renewal results only for the self-similar laws used, not the full cited renewal theorem. Author checks are not independent review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override. The general profile-separation theorem explicitly requires a common Frostman exponent 0<s<1; no unrestricted all-dimension or arbitrary-measure reconstruction claim is made.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: First arXiv submission, distinguished from later revision and discovery dates.

recordDecisions.title: Further spherical Ramsey constructions and classification corollaries
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Strinz’s spherical-ramsey release reports that algebraic concyclic points plus at most three arbitrary points on the same circle are Ramsey, a nine-point radian progression is Ramsey exactly when exp(i theta) is algebraic, and a union of two Möbius images of finite algebraic spherical sets is Ramsey for dimensions>=2. The first two have reported Lean endpoints; the arbitrary-dimensional two-group argument is written/AI-reviewed. The already-counted Möbius-invariance theorem4007 is not a new result here.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The original release directly credits Claude Opus5.5 and Sonnet5.5 with mathematical claims, Lean proofs, certificates and reviews under Will Strinz’s direction.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Use the corrected v1.1.0 credit and scope, not withdrawn v1.0 novelty language about seven generic S2 points. Separate LEAN, exact-certificate-plus-glue, HAND and PROBE levels; finite-field probes are not proofs. The standalone algebraic-plus-three port changes no theorem and is not another discovery. Establish historical priority, dependency on OpenAI172 and first release visibility. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Version1.0.0 archive created October14; corrected version1.1.0 created October15.

recordDecisions.title: An independent integral-tail-signature Hilbert–Smith proof package
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Dabrowski’s source reports an integral-signature-tail p-adic-exclusion argument and Hilbert–Smith conclusion for second-countable locally compact Hausdorff groups acting faithfully and continuously on connected Hausdorff second-countable finite-dimensional boundaryless manifolds, with the Lie structure on the existing topology. The formal statement retains all second-countability assumptions.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The source paper credits human-guided Anthropic, OpenAI and open-source LLM work at nearly every stage, Opus5.5/GPT6.1 on critical constructions, and Opus5.5 for the Lean formalization.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit controlled localization, divisibility and realization of the signature tail, the actual manifold model and statement correspondence. This is a separately authored integral-tail proof package, not verification of OpenAI3891 or the removal of second countability. Establish independence/priority and earliest public visibility; packaging and checker reports are not independent human proof review. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: New reversible quantum-circuit architectures and resource improvements
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Gu, Kemeny, Yelin and Lukin report seven coherent computational-primitive circuit designs improving both Toffoli and peak-qubit counts over their cited baselines, and a new branch-decoding architecture that makes prime-field divsteps inversion practical without retaining a full branch-history stack. The point-addition designs expand the stated qubit/Toffoli trade-off; other tasks use their specified precision and failure budgets. These are constructions and branch-recovery mathematics, not a proof of global resource optimality.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The paper describes evaluator-guided LLM circuit development; the dated Anthropic primary announcement names Claude Mythos5 and attributes new algebraic branch-decoding identities and largely autonomous circuit design, with human task specifications and review.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit the exact branch-decoding theorem and coherent phase/uncomputation correctness, rare-input failure budgets, circuit/resource accounting and comparisons. An independent evaluator is not an independent specialist audit; benchmark scores alone are not the inclusion basis. Do not transfer a selected17x gate comparison or12x decoding gain to every task or promise a practical quantum advantage. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: First arXiv submission, distinguished from later revision and discovery dates.

recordDecisions.title: Exact reconstruction of fourteen standardized elliptic-curve seeds and six base points
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Anthropic reports deterministic lrand48-state/timestamp recipes reproducing ten prime-field and four binary-field published curve seeds, and FreeLIP/NTL generator recipes reproducing six published prime-curve base points. The B-163 seed, the larger NIST prime base points, binary base points and the reasons some candidate curves were skipped remain unexplained. Matching recipes are exact computational constructions, not proof of the historical designers’ intent or of cryptographic security.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The dated primary report credits Claude with recovering the generator patterns, timestamps and selected base-point constructions, under an Anthropic team’s investigation.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently compare the published standard values and recipes without treating matching code as historical documentation. Check the binary half-timestamp interpretation, candidate indexing and omitted cases. This is not an ECDSA break, a security recommendation or a claim that every standardized curve’s origins are known. No downloaded reproduction code was executed. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Preserve provisional=1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Let C=2^(2^(2^87640)). The current owner source reports that for N>=2^C at least N/C starting values n<N reach1 within floor(10.46 log n) ordinary Collatz steps, with a reported odd-start strengthened version also bounded by floor(3.4881 log n) accelerated steps. For every positive t not divisible by3 and N>=2^(t^3 C), at least N/(t^4 C) odd starts n<N reach t within floor(10.46 log(n/t)) ordinary steps and its odd part within floor(3.4881 log(n/t)) accelerated steps. This is positive density with enormous explicit constants, not density one or the full Collatz conjecture.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The new Axiom Math package credits AxiomProver with Lean generation; Kenny Lau checked its formal challenge against the paper. This supplements, not replaces, the original Mazur/OpenAI/Claude research attribution.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit exact tower constants, odd-start/odd-target conventions, ordinary versus accelerated clocks and arbitrary-target normalization. This is an owner-reported formal checkpoint and scope extension, not independent end-to-end verification here. No source code was executed; retain provisional1, low strict confidence, unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The current source reports canonical probe-then-repair dynamic MCS orders after one edge insertion or deletion. The first potentially invalid pick is localized between the endpoints, but the repaired suffix may extend beyond that window. In the stated unit-cost query model the update costs at most n insertion units or n+1 deletion units. A sufficient neighbour-count difference bound only along proper common MCS prefixes gives a common MCS order; insertion/deletion of a matching and a single-edge flip are corollaries. This is not a sublinear worst-case runtime claim.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The reread owner source retains the original disclosed DeepSeek, Claude and Qwen roles; the revised prefix-level argument is not a new autonomous attribution.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit the weaker proper-common-prefix hypothesis and the genuine matching corollary, executable/canonical-order correspondence and unit-cost model. Do not state that every changed suffix position stays inside the endpoint window. Compare the current c4c2c0f revision with the original a872fdd release; preserve the original first-public date and provisional status. No independent human proof review or artifact execution was performed.
